structure.note: Class B shares carry ten votes each and Class A one vote. The FY2024 10-K says Mark Zuckerberg 'is able to exercise voting rights with respect to a majority of the voting power of our outstanding capital stock'. The 2025 proxy gives him 61.0% of total voting power and 99.8% of Class B.

Cash, stock-comp and geography figures come from Meta's own PDF of its FY2024 annual report (Form 10-K, as hosted on Meta's investor CDN), and the cash and stock-comp values were checked against SEC XBRL for the FY2024 10-K (accession 0001326801-25-000017). Buybacks are cash paid in 2024 ($30,125m); the earnings release figure of $29.75 billion is repurchases executed, a different basis. Dividends include dividend equivalents on RSUs. Europe includes Russia and Turkey; Rest of World includes Africa, Latin America and the Middle East (10-K footnote). United States alone was $59.73 billion. OWNERSHIP, PARTLY UNVERIFIED: the 2025 proxy (DEF 14A, accession 0001326801-25-000040) could only be read through the WebFetch tool's page summary before access to www.sec.gov was refused for this session, and that summary cut off before the 5%-holder rows and Zuckerberg's footnote (2). The Zuckerberg row is internally consistent: 342,606,985 / 343,179,151 Class B = 99.83%, and (10 x Class B + Class A) / total votes = 61.04%, matching the stated 99.8 and 61.0. But it has not been checked against the raw page, so both sources carry verified:false. pctEconomic is null because the proxy states class percentages and voting power, not a percentage of all shares; the derived 13.58% is shown separately for an editor to approve. Footnote (2) to the Zuckerberg row was not read, so how his beneficial holding is made up is not recorded. largestHolders is null (not sourced), not empty: the proxy's 5% holder rows could not be read. No employee stock purchase plan appears in the 10-K, so plan is null.
